o.text: Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish اكلمق (aŋlamaq), اكلمخ (aŋlamaḫ, “to understand; to listen”), from Early Old Oghuz اَنْكْلاماقْ (añlamaq, “to understand”) which was a word used only by Oghuz Turks (according to Kaşgari).
From Russian эта́п (etáp). Doublet of etap.
Onomatopoeic. Equivalent to mız (“mumbling sound”) + -ılda (verb forming suffix).
Borrowed from Classical Persian شَلْغَم (šalġam, “turnip”), from Middle Persian [script needed] (SLKʾ /⁠šalgam⁠/), possibly from Ancient Greek σικελικόν (sikelikón, literally “the Sicilian one”).
